headline: SK hynix raises $26.5 billion in U.S. IPO
summary: SK hynix's Nasdaq debut raises record $26.5 billion
details: SK hynix has completed the largest-ever foreign company IPO in U.S. history, raising $26.5 billion in its Nasdaq debut on July 10. The South Korean memory giant sold 177.9 million American depositary receipts (ADRs) at $149 apiece.

The offering was more than seven times oversubscribed and drew demand from more than 500 investment firms. Temporary Nasdaq trading is underway under the ticker SKHYV before regular-way trading begins as SKHY on Monday, July 13.

SK hynix is the world's leading maker of high-bandwidth memory (HBM), critical infrastructure for AI accelerators. The company will steer the proceeds toward boosting its AI-memory manufacturing capacity.

The company is constructing its first U.S. production site, a $4 billion advanced-packaging plant in West Lafayette, Indiana, targeted for completion around 2028. The facility is eligible for up to $458 million in CHIPS Act grants and up to $570 million in federal loans.
caption:
Can $26.5 billion fuel SK hynix's AI memory dominance?

SK hynix has completed the largest-ever foreign company IPO in U.S. history, raising $26.5 billion in its Nasdaq debut on July 10. The South Korean memory giant sold 177.9 million American depositary receipts (ADRs) at $149 apiece.

The offering was more than seven times oversubscribed and drew demand from more than 500 investment firms. Temporary Nasdaq trading is underway under the ticker SKHYV before regular-way trading begins as SKHY on Monday, July 13.

SK hynix is the world's leading maker of high-bandwidth memory (HBM), critical infrastructure for AI accelerators. The company will steer the proceeds toward boosting its AI-memory manufacturing capacity.

The company is constructing its first U.S. production site, a $4 billion advanced-packaging plant in West Lafayette, Indiana, targeted for completion around 2028. The facility is eligible for up to $458 million in CHIPS Act grants and up to $570 million in federal loans.
